system.name: SAGE (Smart Any-horizon aGEnt)
system.one_liner: A video-reasoning agent whose orchestrator answers short videos in one turn and long videos through multi-turn tool calls, trained with synthetic data and RL.

content.variant_note: two worked questions (long video, short video), each setting a human's jumping timeline against SAGE's colour-coded tool-call chain
content.argues: SAGE reasons like a human: iteratively with tool calls on a long video, and in a single pass on a short one.
content.subject: A question about the Ferrari livery in a two-hour video and one about a short clip, each answered by a human and by SAGE.

layout.arrangement_note: Two panels stacked top to bottom, long video (a) and short video (b). Each opens with Intent and Video Context boxes, then two framed lanes: a red Humans lane and a dark-teal SAGE (ours) lane. In (a) the SAGE lane is a snake-shaped chain of seven tool-call blocks; in (b) a mosaic of frames goes straight to Answer Prediction.

encoding.color_means: Colour follows the reasoning turn: orange = turn 1, blue = turn 2, red = turn 3. The same colour marks the human's action arrow, the found entity in the note, the thumbnail outline and timestamp, and SAGE's calls #1, #2, #3. Dark teal = system, intent and answer; red frame = humans.
encoding.line_style_means: no dashed lines; arrow colour gives the turn
encoding.shape_means: tab on a box = its role (Intent, Video Context, Humans, SAGE); small square on the timeline = a visited position; rounded coloured block = one tool call; dark-teal block = the answer
encoding.marker_means: Action-n = the human's n-th jump; #n on a tool call = its turn; timestamps = position in the video
encoding.emphasis: SAGE (ours) sits in a heavier dark frame, and one colour scheme ties each human step to the tool calls that do the same job; the short panel (one arrow) contrasts with the long chain above.

lessons.what_to_learn: Motivate an agent design by drawing a human doing the task and the agent doing it in two aligned frames, and give each reasoning turn one colour reused on the human's arrows and notes, the thumbnails and the agent's tool calls. A second, trivial panel (one arrow) shows the same system skipping the loop on the easy case.
lessons.suits: Agent or multi-turn systems motivated by human behaviour, especially tool-call traces over long media where a short counter-case shows the loop being skipped.

evidence: when viewing a 2-hour-long video, as humans, we take an iterative approach to finding the target information (Fig. 1)
a user would usually ask: ”How does the Ferrari livery look this year?” as an open-ended question

summary: SAGE (Smart Any-horizon aGEnt) is a video-reasoning agent whose orchestrator answers short videos in a single turn and long videos through multi-turn tool calls (web search, video-part extraction, analysis). Figure 1 motivates this by imitating human behaviour in two stacked panels. In (a), a question about the Ferrari livery in a two-hour video is answered by a human who jumps along a timeline (Action-1 to Action-3, with thought notes) and by SAGE as a snake-shaped chain of coloured tool-call blocks ending in Answer Prediction. In (b), a short clip needs one action from the human and one pass over sampled frames for SAGE. One colour per turn links arrows, notes, thumbnails and tool calls.
summary_zh: SAGE 是长视频推理智能体：短视频一轮作答，长视频多轮调用工具。图 1 分上下两栏：(a) 长视频中人沿时间轴三次跳转，SAGE 以同色工具调用链作答；(b) 短视频里两者都一步完成。按轮次着色对应箭头、笔记、缩略图与调用。
notes: Prior labels kept. The SAGE chain could be read as a stage-pipeline, but it is one run's trace, so it is recorded under worked-walkthrough and the typed-trace-blocks tag. Picture counts follow the digest (15 placed tiles: 4 human thumbnails, 3 repeats beside SAGE, 2 sampled-frame strips, 1 start thumbnail and a 5-tile film strip in (b)); the mapping of sizes to items is my reading. The Humans lane illustrates how a person would search, as the paper describes it; the text does not say it is a measured run.
